openings.title: Police hold-period and transaction-reporting compliance log for pawn shops

card.reachableChannel: Shop emails from the state pawnbroker licence register
card.offerScope: Police hold-period and transaction-reporting compliance log for pawn shops

links.basis: reach: Shop emails from the state pawnbroker licence register
price 400 USD is a guess (ASSUMPTION), not something buyers are shown to pay
measured on this offer's own sales: 9 accepted of 90 contacts
7 deal(s) needed, 8680 available in the window (310 reachable buyers, each buying about every 1 days, so 28 purchase(s) each in 28 days)
5 days to usable cash against 28 left

facts.value: 310 pawnbrokers hold state licences; each must report transactions to police daily and keep hold-period logs for inspection.
Sell Police hold-period and transaction-reporting compliance log for pawn shops to each buyer.
A pawnbroker the owner knows said shops would pay $400 for the log.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with OFFER_AND_PRICE decisive is right: the only price ($400) is a PERSON fact - one pawnbroker the owner knows saying shops would pay it - and Brain's own link marks it a guess; someone's word is not a purchase price and one shop is not the 310-licensee population. No agreement is recorded. All other links are evidenced (310 licensed pawnbrokers via the register, 9/90 conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet $5, $0 exposure, 5 days to cash). Owner hours: 0.5 h per deal x 7 deals = 3.5 h across 4 weeks, under 3 h/week. Arithmetic: at $400, 7 deals x ($400-$5) = $2,765 >= $2,400; at 10% conversion that is ~70 contacts of 310. The gap is stated as a gap, not a constraint, which is correct.
findings: The resolution's first route - 'published prices of comparable pawn compliance tools' - is a benchmark of what other sellers charge and cannot establish what these buyers pay; only its second route (a paid order at a stated price from a register-listed pawnbroker) closes OFFER_AND_PRICE. The next revision should make the priced-offer test the resolution, with proof (N paid orders at $400 from the first ~70 contacts), stop and continue rules.
The '>= $370 net' threshold is right for 7 deals ($2,590) but 6 deals need >= $405 gross; state it as ceil($2,400/(P-$5)) deals.
Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis ('each buying about every 1 days, so 28 purchases each') is implausible for a one-time log; the plan correctly needs only one purchase per shop.
Card inconsistency: 9 agreements from 90 contacts are said to be measured on this offer, yet no agreed price is recorded.
